intro.data: Three real steps run A→B→C→D, and the tray holds pre-bundles too — 'Parse+Chart' does the first two at once, 'Chart+Report' the last two. Bring whatever faithful pieces you like from the tray onto the board and wire a route to the true report: all three steps, or a bundle plus a step. Associativity says HOW you group them never changes the result. Two bundles are buggy and produce junk — leave those in the tray.
intro.alchemy: Three real steps run A→B→C→D, and the tray holds pre-bundles too — 'Smelt+Shape' does the first two, 'Shape+Cast' the last two. Bring whatever faithful pieces you like from the tray onto the board and wire a route to the true alloy. Associativity says the grouping never changes the result. Two bundles are botched — leave those in the tray.
intro.spellcraft: Three real steps run A→B→C→D, and the tray holds pre-bundles too — 'Tame+Kindle' does the first two, 'Kindle+Bind' the last two. Bring whatever faithful pieces you like from the tray onto the board and wire a route to the true ward. Associativity says the grouping never changes the result. Two bundles are broken — leave those in the tray.
intro.abstract: Values are plain numbers: f sends 2 ↦ 3, g sends 3 ↦ 6, h sends 6 ↦ 16, so 2 → 3 → 6 → 16 reaches the same 16 however you group it. The tray also holds bundles g∘f (2 ↦ 6) and h∘g (3 ↦ 16), plus buggy look-alikes (2 ↦ 10 and 3 ↦ 40). Bring any faithful grouping from the tray and wire 2 to 16, leaving the buggy bundles in the tray.

afterSuccess.data: However you grouped the faithful steps — all three separately, or with a pre-bundle — you got the same true report. That's associativity: f then (g then h) equals (f then g) then h. The buggy bundles had the right types but the wrong behavior, so they fell out.
afterSuccess.alchemy: However you grouped the faithful steps, you reached the same true alloy. That's associativity: regrouping never changes the result. The botched bundles had the right types but wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: However you grouped the faithful steps, you reached the same true ward. That's associativity: regrouping never changes the result. The broken bundles had the right types but wrong behavior.
afterSuccess.abstract: Every faithful grouping produced D's value: h ∘ (g ∘ f) = (h ∘ g) ∘ f. Associativity lets you bundle freely; only behavior-correct steps qualify.

reveal.summary: Associativity: h ∘ (g ∘ f) = (h ∘ g) ∘ f. You can compose a chain in any grouping and get the same morphism — so a pre-bundled sub-step is interchangeable with doing its steps one by one.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: h(g(f(x))) — where you put the parentheses doesn't change the answer.
